ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the upper +5 V is connected to the collector of Q1 through a 1 kΩ resistor, and the output Vo is taken from this collector node. The base of Q1 is driven by the signal source Vs, and the lower end of the signal source is grounded. The emitter of Q1 is connected to the emitter node of the lower transistor Q2. The left side of the base of Q2 is connected to a bypass capacitor to ground, and is connected to -5 V through RB2; the lower end of Q2 is connected to -5 V. Reasoning: In the mid-frequency small-signal equivalent circuit, the power supply terminals are AC ground, and the bypass capacitor is approximately short-circuited, so the base of Q2 is AC ground. The bias collector currents of both transistors are 2.6 mA, and the thermal voltage is 26 mV, so gm1 = gm2 = Ic/VT = 2.6 mA / 26 mV = 0.1 S. Since the base of Q2 is AC grounded, the small-signal equivalent resistance looking into its emitter is 1/gm2 = 10 Ω. Let the small-signal voltage of the emitter node connecting Q1 and Q2 be ve, and the base voltage of Q1 be vs. The small-signal current injected by Q1 into the emitter node is gm1(vs - ve), and the small-signal current absorbed by Q2 from this node is gm2 ve. From KCL, gm1(vs - ve) = gm2 ve. Because gm1 = gm2, vs - ve = ve, that is, ve = vs/2. Thus the small-signal collector current of Q1 is gm1(vs - ve) = gm1·vs/2. The output is generated on the 1 kΩ collector resistor, so the magnitude of the voltage gain is |Vo/Vs| = Rc·gm1/2 = 1000 × 0.1 / 2 = 50.

method.method_draft: Convert the circuit to its mid-band small-signal equivalent. From the text, compute gm1 = gm2 = 2.6 mA / 26 mV = 0.1 S. Since Q2 base is AC grounded, its emitter node draws small-signal current gm2*ve, so it behaves like a 10 Ω resistance to ground. For Q1, with base voltage vs and emitter voltage ve, collector current is gm1(vs - ve). Apply KCL at the emitter node: current from Q1 into the node equals current into Q2, so gm1(vs - ve) = gm2 ve. With equal gm values, ve = vs/2 and Q1 collector current = gm1*vs/2. The output at the collector across the 1 kΩ resistor has magnitude |v0/vs| = Rc*gm1/2 = 100/2 = 50.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown, transistors \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are biased at a collector current of 2.6 mA. Assuming that transistor current gains are sufficiently large so that collector current can be taken equal to emitter current, and the thermal voltage is 26 mV, the magnitude of voltage gain \(\frac{V_0}{V_s}\) in the mid-band frequency range is _________ (up to second decimal place).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the upper +5 V is connected to the collector of Q1 through a 1 kΩ resistor, and the output Vo is taken from this collector node. The base of Q1 is driven by the signal source Vs, and the lower end of the signal source is grounded. The emitter of Q1 is connected to the emitter node of the lower transistor Q2. The left side of the base of Q2 is connected to a bypass capacitor to ground, and is connected to -5 V through RB2; the lower end of Q2 is connected to -5 V. Reasoning: In the mid-frequency small-signal equivalent circuit, the power supply terminals are AC ground, and the bypass capacitor is approximately short-circuited, so the base of Q2 is AC ground. The bias collector currents of both transistors are 2.6 mA, and the thermal voltage is 26 mV, so gm1 = gm2 = Ic/VT = 2.6 mA / 26 mV = 0.1 S. Since the base of Q2 is AC grounded, the small-signal equivalent resistance looking into its emitter is 1/gm2 = 10 Ω. Let the small-signal voltage of the emitter node connecting Q1 and Q2 be ve, and the base voltage of Q1 be vs. The small-signal current injected by Q1 into the emitter node is gm1(vs - ve), and the small-signal current absorbed by Q2 from this node is gm2 ve. From KCL, gm1(vs - ve) = gm2 ve. Because gm1 = gm2, vs - ve = ve, that is, ve = vs/2. Thus the small-signal collector current of Q1 is gm1(vs - ve) = gm1·vs/2. The output is generated on the 1 kΩ collector resistor, so the magnitude of the voltage gain is |Vo/Vs| = Rc·gm1/2 = 1000 × 0.1 / 2 = 50.
